title: Passkey sign-in with WebAuthn
scenario: Phished passwords and SIM-swapped SMS codes drained 14 accounts; customers want to sign in with a fingerprint or face.
stack: Spring Boot 4.1.1 · Java 25 · WebAuthn with webauthn4j 0.31.9 · TOTP (RFC 6238) · Spring Security 7 resource server · JdbcClient · PostgreSQL 17 · Testcontainers
simulation: Customers and balances are demo rows in a table, not Tijori's; no bank is involved. In the tests, webauthn4j's emulator plays the phone's authenticator and browser, with real keys and real signatures. The TOTP secret is RFC 6238's published test secret, demo only.

Level 1, about 5 minutes. Plain language: no code.

The problem in real life

  1. Phished and SIM-swapped

    Fake Tijori pages collected passwords, and attackers moved customers' numbers to new SIM cards to receive their SMS codes. Fourteen accounts were drained.

  2. Passkeys, half done

    The first passkey code only checked the signature. A sign-in recorded once could be sent again, and an answer made for a look-alike page was accepted.

  3. The fix

    Every sign-in signs a fresh challenge from Tijori, on Tijori's page, for Tijori's domain, with the customer's fingerprint or face. The server checks all of it. The fallback is a password with an authenticator-app code, never SMS.

A signature only proves the key signed something. What it signed, and for whom, is the server's to check.

What are we building?

Passkey registration and sign-in (two ceremonies, each with options and an answer), a password-plus-code fallback, and an account page.

An everyday analogy

A notary stamps a letter only after reading today's date and the addressee aloud. A stamped letter dated last week, or addressed to the shop next door, is worth nothing here, however real the stamp.

How it works in 4 steps

  1. Options: Tijori sends a fresh challenge and its domain.
  2. Phone: the customer touches the sensor; the phone signs the challenge together with the page's origin and the domain.
  3. Check: Tijori uses up the challenge, then checks origin, domain, fingerprint flag, signature and counter.
  4. Token: a 10-minute access token that records how the customer signed in.
Check yourself: why can a fake page not simply pass the customer's passkey answer on to Tijori?

The answer names the page that asked it, inside the signed data. Tijori accepts only its own origin, so an answer made on tijori-login.example is refused, as aSignInAnsweredForAPhishingPageIsRefused shows. (Real browsers also refuse to use a Tijori passkey on another domain at all.)

What this station is not

  • No real phone in the tests. webauthn4j's emulator plays it, with real keys.
  • No attestation checks. Tijori does not ask which model of authenticator made the key (attestation: none).
  • No account recovery. Losing every passkey and the code app is a support process (Practice, challenge 3).

Level 2. What a teammate hands you before you build.

Business problem

Tijori (a fictional bank) lost 14 accounts to phished passwords and SIM-swapped SMS codes; customers want to sign in with a fingerprint or face.

Acceptance criteria

Demo data: customers zoya and dev, with passwords and the same demo TOTP secret.

  1. Given the right password and the current code, then 200 with a token; the same code again is 401.
  2. Given a sign-in from the last 5 minutes, then a passkey can be registered; with an older token, 403.
  3. Given a registered passkey and a fresh challenge on Tijori's page, then sign-in works without a password.
  4. Given a sign-in answer sent twice, made for another page, or made for another domain, then it is refused.
  5. Given a passkey answer claiming another customer, or a registration on another customer's challenge, then refused.
  6. Given ten sign-ins with one code at once, then exactly one token.

Requirements

  • The challenge, origin and RP id come from the server, never from the request.
  • Challenges are single-use and last 5 minutes; the database enforces their shape and lifetime.
  • No SMS anywhere. A password is never enough on its own.

Learning objectives

  • Run both WebAuthn ceremonies and name every server-side check.
  • Explain what makes passkeys resistant to phishing, and what the server still has to do.
  • Implement TOTP with single use and a small time window.
  • Test with an authenticator emulator instead of a phone.

From psql in docs/capture.sh.

----------------+----------------+-----------+------

The trap

Plausible but wrong

Not checking the challenge, origin and relying-party id, so a phishing site can replay a sign-in.

The old code checked only that the signature matched the stored public key. Each test makes one answer it accepted:

  • Replayed. A real sign-in, sent again a minute later: the signature is still valid. The API refuses it, because its challenge was used up. The test device keeps its counter at 0, as synced passkeys commonly do, so only the challenge stops this.
  • Answered for a phishing page. tijori-login.example fetches a real challenge and gets the passkey to answer it on its own page: valid signature, wrong origin. Refused.
  • Made for another site. A look-alike page asks for a passkey for its own domain and hands it to Tijori. The old code stored any key it could parse. Refused.
  • The control. A fresh challenge on Tijori's page signs in.

While building, each check was undone once: the sign-in challenge taken from the request turned 3 tests red; any origin 1; no userHandle comparison 1; no owner check on the registration challenge 1; registration without its transaction 1, or rolling back on every failure 1; no recent sign-in check 1; a reusable code 2; no one-step window 1; the counter not stored 1. Not requiring user verification turned nothing red: the emulator always reports it.

package com.tijori.passkeys;

import com.webauthn4j.WebAuthnManager;
import com.webauthn4j.converter.AttestedCredentialDataConverter;
import com.webauthn4j.converter.util.ObjectConverter;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import tools.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode;

import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream;
import java.security.MessageDigest;
import java.security.Signature;
import java.util.Base64;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.status;

/**
 * Written first. The old passkey code checked only the signature with the stored public key: not which challenge was
 * signed, not which page asked, not which site the passkey was made for. Each test builds one answer the old code
 * accepted, then sends it to the real API.
 */
class UncheckedCeremonyTrapTest extends ApiTest {

    static final Base64.Decoder UNB64 = Base64.getUrlDecoder();

    /** The old sign-in check, as it was: is this a valid signature by the stored key? */
    boolean oldSignatureOnlyCheck(JsonNode assertion) throws Exception {
        byte[] stored = jdbc.sql("SELECT attested_credential_data FROM passkeys WHERE credential_id = ?")
                .param(UNB64.decode(assertion.path("rawId").asString())).query(byte[].class).single();
        var key = new AttestedCredentialDataConverter(new ObjectConverter()).convert(stored).getCOSEKey().getPublicKey();
        JsonNode r = assertion.path("response");
        ByteArrayOutputStream signed = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
        signed.write(UNB64.decode(r.path("authenticatorData").asString()));
        signed.write(MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256").digest(UNB64.decode(r.path("clientDataJSON").asString())));
        Signature verifier = Signature.getInstance("SHA256withECDSA");
        verifier.initVerify(key);
        verifier.update(signed.toByteArray());
        return verifier.verify(UNB64.decode(r.path("signature").asString()));
    }

    @Test
    void aSignInCapturedOnceAndSentAgainIsRefused() throws Exception {
        Device phone = passkeyFor("zoya");
        ObjectNode signIn = phone.get(authenticationOptions());
        authenticate(signIn).andExpect(status().isOk());
        // Captured from a log or a proxy: the very same answer, a minute later. A synced passkey's counter stays 0,
        // so only the used-up challenge stops it.
        later(java.time.Duration.ofMinutes(1));
        assertThat(oldSignatureOnlyCheck(signIn)).isTrue();             // the old code: signed in again
        authenticate(signIn).andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());      // its challenge was used up
    }

    @Test
    void aSignInAnsweredForAPhishingPageIsRefused() throws Exception {
        Device phone = passkeyFor("zoya");
        // tijori-login.example fetches a real challenge from Tijori and gets the passkey to answer it on its own page.
        ObjectNode relayed = phone.at("https://tijori-login.example").get(authenticationOptions());
        assertThat(oldSignatureOnlyCheck(relayed)).isTrue();
        authenticate(relayed).andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());     // clientDataJSON names the page that asked
    }

    @Test
    void aPasskeyMadeForAnotherSiteIsNotRegistered() throws Exception {
        String token = codeToken("zoya");
        // A look-alike page asks for a passkey for its own relying party, then hands the result to Tijori.
        ObjectNode forOtherSite = new Device().create(registrationOptions(token), "tijori-login.example");
        assertThat(WebAuthnManager.createNonStrictWebAuthnManager().parseRegistrationResponseJSON(forOtherSite.toString())).isNotNull();   // the old code stored any parsable key
        register(token, "Zoya's phone", forOtherSite).andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
        assertThat(jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM passkeys").query(Long.class).single()).isZero();
    }

    @Test
    void theRightAnswerSignsIn() throws Exception {
        // The control: same passkey, Tijori's own page, a fresh challenge.
        Device phone = passkeyFor("zoya");
        authenticate(phone.get(authenticationOptions())).andExpect(status().isOk());
    }
}

src/main/java/com/tijori/passkeys/SecurityConfig.java

Does
Who may call what.
Why
The sign-in ceremonies and the code sign-in are open (they are the proof); adding a passkey and the account need a token; everything else refused.
Without it
A passkey added by someone who is not signed in, or a new endpoint open by default.
package com.tijori.passkeys;

import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.http.HttpMethod;
import org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.builders.HttpSecurity;
import org.springframework.security.config.http.SessionCreationPolicy;
import org.springframework.security.crypto.factory.PasswordEncoderFactories;
import org.springframework.security.crypto.password.PasswordEncoder;
import org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain;

@Configuration
class SecurityConfig {

    /** The sign-in ceremonies are open (they are the proof); adding a passkey and the account need a token. */
    @Bean
    SecurityFilterChain api(HttpSecurity http, ProblemResponses problems) throws Exception {
        http.authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a
                        .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.POST, "/2fa/totp", "/webauthn/authentication/options", "/webauthn/authentication").permitAll()
                        .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.POST, "/webauthn/registration/options", "/webauthn/registration").hasAuthority("SCOPE_accounts")
                        .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/accounts/me").hasAuthority("SCOPE_accounts")
                        .requestMatchers("/error").permitAll()   // otherwise a server error is forwarded here and shown as a 401
                        .anyRequest().denyAll())
                .oauth2ResourceServer(o -> o.jwt(jwt -> {}).authenticationEntryPoint(problems::unauthenticated).accessDeniedHandler(problems::forbidden))
                .exceptionHandling(x -> x.authenticationEntryPoint(problems::unauthenticated).accessDeniedHandler(problems::forbidden))
                .sessionManagement(s -> s.sessionCreationPolicy(SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS))
                .csrf(csrf -> csrf.disable());   // no cookies: the token travels in a header the browser never adds by itself
        return http.build();
    }

    @Bean
    PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder() {
        return PasswordEncoderFactories.createDelegatingPasswordEncoder();
    }
}

Does
The five sign-in endpoints.
Why
Password and code together, never apart; adding a passkey needs a sign-in from the last 5 minutes; one answer for every failed ceremony.
Without it
A stolen token planting the attacker's own passkey, or errors that tell which check failed.
package com.tijori.passkeys;

import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Email;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Pattern;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Size;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.security.core.annotation.AuthenticationPrincipal;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.jwt.Jwt;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ExceptionHandler;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;
import org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException;
import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;

import java.net.URI;
import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

@RestController
class SignInController {

    record CodeLogin(@NotBlank @Email @Size(max = 254) String email, @NotNull @Size(min = 1, max = 64) String password,
                     @NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "\\d{6}") String code) {
    }

    record NewPasskey(@NotBlank @Size(max = 60) String label, @NotNull JsonNode credential) {
    }

    /** Demo rule: adding a passkey needs a sign-in from the last 5 minutes, so a stolen token cannot plant one. */
    static final Duration RECENT_SIGN_IN = Duration.ofMinutes(5);

    private final CodeSignIn codes;
    private final Passkeys passkeys;
    private final TokenService tokens;
    private final Clock clock;

    SignInController(CodeSignIn codes, Passkeys passkeys, TokenService tokens, Clock clock) {
        this.codes = codes;
        this.passkeys = passkeys;
        this.tokens = tokens;
        this.clock = clock;
    }

    @PostMapping("/2fa/totp")
    TokenService.AccessToken codeSignIn(@Valid @RequestBody CodeLogin body) {
        long customer = codes.signIn(body.email(), body.password(), body.code())
                .orElseThrow(() -> new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED, "Wrong email, password or code"));
        return tokens.issue(customer, List.of("pwd", "otp", "mfa"));
    }

    @PostMapping("/webauthn/registration/options")
    Map<String, Object> registrationOptions(@AuthenticationPrincipal Jwt jwt) {
        return passkeys.registrationOptions(recentlySignedIn(jwt));
    }

    @PostMapping("/webauthn/registration")
    ResponseEntity<Map<String, String>> register(@AuthenticationPrincipal Jwt jwt, @Valid @RequestBody NewPasskey body) {
        String id = passkeys.register(recentlySignedIn(jwt), body.label(), body.credential());
        return ResponseEntity.created(URI.create("/webauthn/passkeys/" + id)).body(Map.of("id", id, "label", body.label().strip()));
    }

    @PostMapping("/webauthn/authentication/options")
    Map<String, Object> authenticationOptions() {
        return passkeys.authenticationOptions();
    }

    @PostMapping("/webauthn/authentication")
    TokenService.AccessToken authenticate(@RequestBody JsonNode credential) {
        return tokens.issue(passkeys.authenticate(credential), List.of("hwk", "user"));
    }

    /** One answer for every failed ceremony; the reason goes to the log. Registration is 400: the caller is known. */
    @ExceptionHandler(Passkeys.CeremonyFailed.class)
    ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail> ceremonyFailed(Passkeys.CeremonyFailed e, HttpServletRequest request) {
        HttpStatus status = request.getRequestURI().startsWith("/webauthn/registration") ? HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST : HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED;
        return ResponseEntity.status(status).body(ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(status, "The passkey check failed. Try again."));
    }

    private long recentlySignedIn(Jwt jwt) {
        if (jwt.getIssuedAt() == null || jwt.getIssuedAt().plus(RECENT_SIGN_IN).isBefore(clock.instant())) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN, "Sign in again to add a passkey");
        }
        return Long.parseLong(jwt.getSubject());
    }

Does
Both WebAuthn ceremonies.
Why
The challenge is ours and used up in one conditional UPDATE; then webauthn4j checks it with our origin and our RP id, user verification, the signature and the counter; the server compares userHandle itself.
Without it
Replays, answers made for other pages or other sites, and one customer's passkey speaking for another.
  • The signature covers the authenticator data and a hash of clientDataJSON, not userHandle: a changed userHandle keeps the signature valid. Found while building.
  • Synced passkeys commonly report a counter of 0, so the counter cannot be relied on to stop replays: the challenge does. Found while building, when the replay test first stayed green.
  • Both ceremonies are transactions with noRollbackFor = CeremonyFailed: a failed check still uses up its challenge, a failed save does not.
package com.tijori.passkeys;

import com.webauthn4j.WebAuthnManager;
import com.webauthn4j.converter.AttestedCredentialDataConverter;
import com.webauthn4j.converter.util.ObjectConverter;
import com.webauthn4j.credential.CredentialRecordImpl;
import com.webauthn4j.data.AuthenticationData;
import com.webauthn4j.data.AuthenticationParameters;
import com.webauthn4j.data.PublicKeyCredentialParameters;
import com.webauthn4j.data.PublicKeyCredentialType;
import com.webauthn4j.data.RegistrationData;
import com.webauthn4j.data.RegistrationParameters;
import com.webauthn4j.data.attestation.authenticator.AttestedCredentialData;
import com.webauthn4j.data.attestation.statement.COSEAlgorithmIdentifier;
import com.webauthn4j.data.attestation.statement.NoneAttestationStatement;
import com.webauthn4j.data.client.Origin;
import com.webauthn4j.data.client.challenge.DefaultChallenge;
import com.webauthn4j.data.extension.authenticator.AuthenticationExtensionsAuthenticatorOutputs;
import com.webauthn4j.data.extension.client.AuthenticationExtensionsClientOutputs;
import com.webauthn4j.server.ServerProperty;
import com.webauthn4j.verifier.exception.VerificationException;
import com.webauthn4j.converter.exception.DataConversionException;
import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;
import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;

import java.security.SecureRandom;
import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.time.OffsetDateTime;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.Base64;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Optional;

/**
 * The two WebAuthn ceremonies. Each starts with a challenge from this server and ends with webauthn4j checking the
 * browser's answer against three values that come from here, never from the request: the challenge we issued, our
 * origin, and our relying-party id. Then the signature, user verification and the signature counter.
 */
@Service
class Passkeys {

    private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(Passkeys.class);
    private static final SecureRandom RANDOM = new SecureRandom();
    private static final JsonMapper JSON = JsonMapper.builder().build();
    private static final Base64.Encoder B64 = Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding();
    private static final Base64.Decoder UNB64 = Base64.getUrlDecoder();
    /** ES256 and RS256: what platform authenticators and security keys offer. */
    static final List<PublicKeyCredentialParameters> ALGORITHMS = List.of(
            new PublicKeyCredentialParameters(PublicKeyCredentialType.PUBLIC_KEY, COSEAlgorithmIdentifier.ES256),
            new PublicKeyCredentialParameters(PublicKeyCredentialType.PUBLIC_KEY, COSEAlgorithmIdentifier.RS256));

    /** The browser's answer failed a check. Which one is logged, not told. */
    static final class CeremonyFailed extends RuntimeException {
        CeremonyFailed(String reason) {
            super(reason);
        }
    }

    private final JdbcClient jdbc;
    private final Clock clock;
    private final String rpId;
    private final String rpName;
    private final Origin origin;
    private final Duration challengeLifetime;
    private final ObjectConverter converter = new ObjectConverter();
    private final WebAuthnManager webAuthn = WebAuthnManager.createNonStrictWebAuthnManager(converter);
    private final AttestedCredentialDataConverter credentialData = new AttestedCredentialDataConverter(converter);

    Passkeys(JdbcClient jdbc, Clock clock, @Value("${tijori.webauthn.rp-id}") String rpId, @Value("${tijori.webauthn.rp-name}") String rpName,
             @Value("${tijori.webauthn.origin}") String origin, @Value("${tijori.webauthn.challenge-lifetime}") Duration challengeLifetime) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
        this.clock = clock;
        this.rpId = rpId;
        this.rpName = rpName;
        this.origin = new Origin(origin);
        this.challengeLifetime = challengeLifetime;
    }

    private record Customer(String email, String name, byte[] userHandle) {
    }

    /** What the browser passes to navigator.credentials.create(), as JSON. */
    Map<String, Object> registrationOptions(long customerId) {
        Customer c = jdbc.sql("SELECT email, name, user_handle FROM customers WHERE id = ?").param(customerId).query(Customer.class).single();
        List<Map<String, String>> existing = jdbc.sql("SELECT credential_id FROM passkeys WHERE customer_id = ?").param(customerId)
                .query(byte[].class).list().stream().map(id -> Map.of("type", "public-key", "id", B64.encodeToString(id))).toList();
        Map<String, Object> options = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        options.put("challenge", newChallenge("registration", customerId));
        options.put("rp", Map.of("id", rpId, "name", rpName));
        options.put("user", Map.of("id", B64.encodeToString(c.userHandle()), "name", c.email(), "displayName", c.name()));
        options.put("pubKeyCredParams", ALGORITHMS.stream().map(p -> Map.of("type", "public-key", "alg", p.getAlg().getValue())).toList());
        options.put("timeout", challengeLifetime.toMillis());
        options.put("excludeCredentials", existing);   // the same authenticator is not registered twice
        options.put("authenticatorSelection", Map.of("residentKey", "required", "userVerification", "required"));
        options.put("attestation", "none");
        return options;
    }

    /**
     * Checks the new passkey and stores its public key. Returns its credential id. One transaction: a failed check
     * still uses up the challenge (no second try with it), but a failed save rolls back, so the same answer can be sent again.
     */
    @Transactional(noRollbackFor = CeremonyFailed.class)
    String register(long customerId, String label, JsonNode credential) {
        byte[] challenge = useChallenge(credential, "registration")
                .filter(owner -> owner == customerId)   // a challenge issued to someone else proves nothing for this customer
                .map(owner -> clientChallenge(credential)).orElseThrow(() -> new CeremonyFailed("unknown, used, expired or someone else's challenge"));
        RegistrationData data;
        try {
            data = webAuthn.verifyRegistrationResponseJSON(credential.toString(),
                    new RegistrationParameters(server(challenge), ALGORITHMS, true, true));
        } catch (VerificationException | DataConversionException e) {
            log.info("Passkey registration refused: {}", e.getClass().getSimpleName());
            throw new CeremonyFailed(e.getClass().getSimpleName());
        }
        AttestedCredentialData acd = data.getAttestationObject().getAuthenticatorData().getAttestedCredentialData();
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO passkeys (credential_id, customer_id, attested_credential_data, sign_count, label, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)")
                .params(acd.getCredentialId(), customerId, credentialData.convert(acd), data.getAttestationObject().getAuthenticatorData().getSignCount(),
                        label.strip(), now()).update();
        return B64.encodeToString(acd.getCredentialId());
    }

    /** What the browser passes to navigator.credentials.get(): no user named, the passkey says who it is. */
    Map<String, Object> authenticationOptions() {
        Map<String, Object> options = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        options.put("challenge", newChallenge("authentication", null));
        options.put("rpId", rpId);
        options.put("timeout", challengeLifetime.toMillis());
        options.put("allowCredentials", List.of());
        options.put("userVerification", "required");
        return options;
    }

    private record Stored(long customerId, byte[] userHandle, byte[] attestedCredentialData, long signCount) {
    }

    /** The customer whose passkey this is, after every check. One transaction, as for registration. */
    @Transactional(noRollbackFor = CeremonyFailed.class)
    long authenticate(JsonNode credential) {
        byte[] challenge = useChallenge(credential, "authentication").map(any -> clientChallenge(credential))
                .orElseThrow(() -> new CeremonyFailed("unknown, used or expired challenge"));
        byte[] credentialId = UNB64.decode(text(credential, "rawId"));
        Stored stored = jdbc.sql("""
                        SELECT p.customer_id, c.user_handle, p.attested_credential_data, p.sign_count
                        FROM passkeys p JOIN customers c ON c.id = p.customer_id WHERE p.credential_id = ?""")
                .param(credentialId).query(Stored.class).optional().orElseThrow(() -> new CeremonyFailed("unknown passkey"));
        // The passkey must also say it belongs to that customer (WebAuthn's userHandle check).
        if (!Arrays.equals(UNB64.decode(text(credential.path("response"), "userHandle")), stored.userHandle())) {
            throw new CeremonyFailed("userHandle does not match the passkey's customer");
        }
        CredentialRecordImpl record = new CredentialRecordImpl(new NoneAttestationStatement(), null, null, null, stored.signCount(),
                credentialData.convert(stored.attestedCredentialData()), new AuthenticationExtensionsAuthenticatorOutputs<>(), null,
                new AuthenticationExtensionsClientOutputs<>(), null);
        AuthenticationData data;
        try {
            data = webAuthn.verifyAuthenticationResponseJSON(credential.toString(),
                    new AuthenticationParameters(server(challenge), record, null, true, true));
        } catch (VerificationException | DataConversionException e) {
            log.info("Passkey sign-in refused: {}", e.getClass().getSimpleName());
            throw new CeremonyFailed(e.getClass().getSimpleName());
        }
        // A counter that goes backwards can mean a cloned authenticator; webauthn4j refuses it above. Store the new one.
        jdbc.sql("UPDATE passkeys SET sign_count = ?, last_used_at = ? WHERE credential_id = ?")
                .params(data.getAuthenticatorData().getSignCount(), now(), credentialId).update();
        return stored.customerId();
    }

    /** Our values, never the request's: the challenge we issued, our origin, our relying-party id. */
    private ServerProperty server(byte[] challenge) {
        return new ServerProperty(origin, rpId, new DefaultChallenge(challenge));
    }

    private String newChallenge(String purpose, Long customerId) {
        byte[] challenge = new byte[32];
        RANDOM.nextBytes(challenge);
        OffsetDateTime created = now();   // one clock read: two would break the 5-minute CHECK
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO webauthn_challenges (challenge, purpose, customer_id, created_at, expires_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)")
                .params(challenge, purpose, customerId, created, created.plus(challengeLifetime)).update();
        return B64.encodeToString(challenge);
    }

    /**
     * Marks the challenge in the browser's clientDataJSON as used, if this server issued it for this purpose and it
     * is unused and in time: one conditional UPDATE, so a challenge works for exactly one answer. Returns its owner
     * (0 for sign-in challenges, which have none).
     */
    private Optional<Long> useChallenge(JsonNode credential, String purpose) {
        byte[] challenge;
        try {
            challenge = clientChallenge(credential);
        } catch (RuntimeException notOurShape) {
            return Optional.empty();
        }
        OffsetDateTime now = now();
        return jdbc.sql("UPDATE webauthn_challenges SET used_at = ? WHERE challenge = ? AND purpose = ? AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > ? RETURNING coalesce(customer_id, 0)")
                .params(now, challenge, purpose, now).query(Long.class).optional();
    }

    private static byte[] clientChallenge(JsonNode credential) {
        JsonNode clientData = JSON.readTree(UNB64.decode(text(credential.path("response"), "clientDataJSON")));
        return UNB64.decode(text(clientData, "challenge"));
    }

    private static String text(JsonNode node, String field) {
        JsonNode value = node.path(field);
        if (!value.isString()) {
            throw new CeremonyFailed("missing " + field);
        }
        return value.asString();
    }

    private OffsetDateTime now() {
        return OffsetDateTime.ofInstant(clock.instant(), ZoneOffset.UTC);
    }
}

Does
The fallback: password and an authenticator-app code.
Why
RFC 6238 codes for the current and the previous 30 seconds, compared in constant time, each accepted once (totp_last_step moves forward in one conditional UPDATE).
Without it

package com.tijori.passkeys;

import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.security.crypto.password.PasswordEncoder;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

import java.security.MessageDigest;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.time.Clock;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Optional;

/** The fallback: password and a code from an authenticator app. Never a password alone, never an SMS. */
@Service
class CodeSignIn {

    private final JdbcClient jdbc;
    private final PasswordEncoder encoder;
    private final Clock clock;
    private final String dummyHash;

    CodeSignIn(JdbcClient jdbc, PasswordEncoder encoder, Clock clock) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
        this.encoder = encoder;
        this.clock = clock;
        this.dummyHash = encoder.encode("no-such-customer");
    }

    private record Customer(long id, String passwordHash, byte[] totpSecret) {
    }

    /**
     * The customer's id if the password is right and the code is the current one (or the one before, for a slow
     * phone clock) and has not been used yet. Using it moves totp_last_step forward in one conditional UPDATE, so
     * of two requests with the same code exactly one gets through.
     */
    Optional<Long> signIn(String email, String password, String code) {
        Optional<Customer> customer = jdbc.sql("SELECT id, password_hash, totp_secret FROM customers WHERE email = ?")
                .param(email.strip().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)).query(Customer.class).optional();
        boolean passwordOk = encoder.matches(password, customer.map(Customer::passwordHash).orElse(dummyHash));
        if (customer.isEmpty() || !passwordOk) {
            return Optional.empty();
        }
        long now = Totp.step(clock.instant().getEpochSecond());
        for (long step = now; step >= now - 1; step--) {
            if (MessageDigest.isEqual(Totp.code(customer.get().totpSecret(), step).getBytes(StandardCharsets.US_ASCII), code.getBytes(StandardCharsets.US_ASCII))) {
                return jdbc.sql("UPDATE customers SET totp_last_step = ? WHERE id = ? AND (totp_last_step IS NULL OR totp_last_step < ?) RETURNING id")
                        .params(step, customer.get().id(), step).query(Long.class).optional();
            }
        }
        return Optional.empty();
    }
}

The code itself: HMAC-SHA1 over the step number, dynamic truncation, six digits.

package com.tijori.passkeys;

import javax.crypto.Mac;
import javax.crypto.spec.SecretKeySpec;
import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
import java.security.GeneralSecurityException;

/** Time-based one-time codes, RFC 6238: HMAC-SHA1 over the 30-second step number, 6 digits. */
final class Totp {

    static final long STEP_SECONDS = 30;

    private Totp() {
    }

    static long step(long epochSecond) {
        return Math.floorDiv(epochSecond, STEP_SECONDS);
    }

    static String code(byte[] secret, long step) {
        try {
            Mac mac = Mac.getInstance("HmacSHA1");
            mac.init(new SecretKeySpec(secret, "HmacSHA1"));
            byte[] h = mac.doFinal(ByteBuffer.allocate(8).putLong(step).array());
            int offset = h[h.length - 1] & 0x0f;   // RFC 4226 dynamic truncation
            int binary = ((h[offset] & 0x7f) << 24) | ((h[offset + 1] & 0xff) << 16) | ((h[offset + 2] & 0xff) << 8) | (h[offset + 3] & 0xff);
            return String.format("%06d", binary % 1_000_000);
        } catch (GeneralSecurityException e) {
            throw new IllegalStateException(e);
        }
    }
}

    record AccessToken(String accessToken, String tokenType, long expiresIn, List<String> signedInWith) {
    }

    private final JwtEncoder encoder;
    private final Clock clock;
    private final String issuer;
    private final String audience;
    private final Duration lifetime;

    TokenService(JwtEncoder encoder, Clock clock, @Value("${tijori.jwt.issuer}") String issuer,

        this.clock = clock;
        this.issuer = issuer;
        this.audience = audience;
        this.lifetime = lifetime;

                .issuer(issuer).subject(Long.toString(customerId)).audience(List.of(audience))
                .issuedAt(now).expiresAt(now.plus(lifetime))
                .claim("scope", "accounts").claim("amr", amr)
                .build();
        String token = encoder.encode(JwtEncoderParameters.from(JwsHeader.with(MacAlgorithm.HS256).build(), claims)).getTokenValue();
        return new AccessToken(token, "Bearer", lifetime.toSeconds(), amr);
    }
}

import org.springframework.security.oauth2.jwt.NimbusJwtEncoder;

import javax.crypto.SecretKey;
import javax.crypto.spec.SecretKeySpec;
import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.util.Base64;
import java.util.List;

/** One HMAC key signs the access tokens issued after a passkey or a password and code, and checks them. */
@Configuration
class JwtConfig {

    @Bean
    SecretKey jwtKey(@Value("${tijori.jwt.secret}") String secret) {
        return new SecretKeySpec(Base64.getUrlDecoder().decode(secret), "HmacSHA256");
    }

    @Bean
    JwtEncoder jwtEncoder(SecretKey key) {
        return new NimbusJwtEncoder(new ImmutableSecret<>(key));
    }

    /**
     * Checks, for every request: the signature with this key and only HS256 (no "none", no other algorithm), the
     * expiry and not-before times with a small allowance for clocks that differ, the issuer and the audience.
     */
    @Bean
    JwtDecoder jwtDecoder(SecretKey key, Clock clock, @Value("${tijori.jwt.issuer}") String issuer,
                          @Value("${tijori.jwt.audience}") String audience, @Value("${tijori.jwt.clock-skew}") Duration skew) {
        NimbusJwtDecoder decoder = NimbusJwtDecoder.withSecretKey(key).macAlgorithm(MacAlgorithm.HS256).build();
        JwtTimestampValidator timestamps = new JwtTimestampValidator(skew);
        timestamps.setClock(clock);
        decoder.setJwtValidator(new DelegatingOAuth2TokenValidator<>(timestamps, new JwtIssuerValidator(issuer),
                new JwtClaimValidator<List<String>>(JwtClaimNames.AUD, aud -> aud != null && aud.contains(audience))));
        return decoder;
    }
}

package com.tijori.passkeys;

import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException;
import org.springframework.security.core.AuthenticationException;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.Map;

/** 401 and 403 from Spring Security's filters, in the same problem shape as every other error. */
@Component
class ProblemResponses {

    private static final JsonMapper JSON = JsonMapper.builder().build();

    /** 401: who are you? No token, or one that is not valid: forged, expired, for another API. One answer for all. */
    void unauthenticated(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, AuthenticationException e) throws IOException {
        res.setHeader("WWW-Authenticate", "Bearer");
        write(req, res, HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED, "Sign-in required", "Send a valid access token: sign in again to get one.");
    }

    /** 403: we know who you are, and you may not do this. */
    void forbidden(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, AccessDeniedException e) throws IOException {
        write(req, res, HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN, "Not allowed", "Sign in again to do this.");
    }

    private static void write(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, HttpStatus status, String title, String detail) throws IOException {
        Map<String, Object> body = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        body.put("title", title);
        body.put("status", status.value());
        body.put("detail", detail);
        body.put("instance", req.getRequestURI());
        res.setStatus(status.value());
        res.setContentType("application/problem+json");
        JSON.writeValue(res.getOutputStream(), body);
    }
}

    id             bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY CONSTRAINT customers_pk PRIMARY KEY,
    email          text NOT NULL,
    name           text NOT NULL,
    -- WebAuthn's user.id: random bytes, never the email, so a passkey reveals nothing about who it belongs to.
    user_handle    bytea NOT NULL,
    password_hash  text NOT NULL,
    totp_secret    bytea NOT NULL,
    -- The last 30-second step whose code was accepted: a code works once.
    totp_last_step bigint,
    balance_paise  bigint NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT customers_email_lower CHECK (email = lower(email)),
    CONSTRAINT customers_email_unique UNIQUE (email),
    CONSTRAINT customers_user_handle_unique UNIQUE (user_handle),
    CONSTRAINT customers_user_handle_length CHECK (octet_length(user_handle) = 32),
    CONSTRAINT customers_password_hash_shape CHECK (password_hash ~ '^\{bcrypt\}\$2[aby]\$(1[0-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\$[./A-Za-z0-9]{53}$'),
    CONSTRAINT customers_totp_secret_length CHECK (octet_length(totp_secret) >= 20),
    CONSTRAINT customers_balance_nonnegative CHECK (balance_paise >= 0)
);

CREATE TABLE passkeys (
    credential_id            bytea CONSTRAINT passkeys_pk PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id              bigint NOT NULL CONSTRAINT passkeys_customer_fk REFERENCES customers ON DELETE CASCADE,
    -- The authenticator's AAGUID, the credential id and the COSE public key, as the authenticator sent them.
    attested_credential_data bytea NOT NULL,
    sign_count               bigint NOT NULL,
    label                    text NOT NULL,
    created_at               timestamptz NOT NULL,
    last_used_at             timestamptz,
    CONSTRAINT passkeys_credential_id_length CHECK (octet_length(credential_id) BETWEEN 16 AND 1023),
    CONSTRAINT passkeys_sign_count_range CHECK (sign_count BETWEEN 0 AND 4294967295),
    CONSTRAINT passkeys_label_length CHECK (char_length(label) BETWEEN 1 AND 60)
);

-- Every ceremony starts with a random challenge from the server; each is good once, for 5 minutes.
CREATE TABLE webauthn_challenges (
    challenge   bytea CONSTRAINT webauthn_challenges_pk PRIMARY KEY,
    purpose     text NOT NULL,
    customer_id bigint CONSTRAINT webauthn_challenges_customer_fk REFERENCES customers ON DELETE CASCADE,
    created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL,
    expires_at  timestamptz NOT NULL,
    used_at     timestamptz,
    CONSTRAINT webauthn_challenges_length CHECK (octet_length(challenge) = 32),
    CONSTRAINT webauthn_challenges_purpose CHECK (purpose IN ('registration', 'authentication')),
    CONSTRAINT webauthn_challenges_registration_has_customer CHECK (purpose <> 'registration' OR customer_id IS NOT NULL),
    CONSTRAINT webauthn_challenges_expiry CHECK (expires_at > created_at AND expires_at <= created_at + interval '5 minutes'),
    CONSTRAINT webauthn_challenges_used_in_time CHECK (used_at IS NULL OR used_at >= created_at)
);

Written first: three answers the signature-only check accepted, each refused by the API, and the control.

package com.tijori.passkeys;

import com.webauthn4j.WebAuthnManager;
import com.webauthn4j.converter.AttestedCredentialDataConverter;
import com.webauthn4j.converter.util.ObjectConverter;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import tools.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode;

import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream;
import java.security.MessageDigest;
import java.security.Signature;
import java.util.Base64;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.status;

/**
 * Written first. The old passkey code checked only the signature with the stored public key: not which challenge was
 * signed, not which page asked, not which site the passkey was made for. Each test builds one answer the old code
 * accepted, then sends it to the real API.
 */
class UncheckedCeremonyTrapTest extends ApiTest {

    static final Base64.Decoder UNB64 = Base64.getUrlDecoder();

    /** The old sign-in check, as it was: is this a valid signature by the stored key? */
    boolean oldSignatureOnlyCheck(JsonNode assertion) throws Exception {
        byte[] stored = jdbc.sql("SELECT attested_credential_data FROM passkeys WHERE credential_id = ?")
                .param(UNB64.decode(assertion.path("rawId").asString())).query(byte[].class).single();
        var key = new AttestedCredentialDataConverter(new ObjectConverter()).convert(stored).getCOSEKey().getPublicKey();
        JsonNode r = assertion.path("response");
        ByteArrayOutputStream signed = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
        signed.write(UNB64.decode(r.path("authenticatorData").asString()));
        signed.write(MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256").digest(UNB64.decode(r.path("clientDataJSON").asString())));
        Signature verifier = Signature.getInstance("SHA256withECDSA");
        verifier.initVerify(key);
        verifier.update(signed.toByteArray());
        return verifier.verify(UNB64.decode(r.path("signature").asString()));
    }

    @Test
    void aSignInCapturedOnceAndSentAgainIsRefused() throws Exception {
        Device phone = passkeyFor("zoya");
        ObjectNode signIn = phone.get(authenticationOptions());
        authenticate(signIn).andExpect(status().isOk());
        // Captured from a log or a proxy: the very same answer, a minute later. A synced passkey's counter stays 0,
        // so only the used-up challenge stops it.
        later(java.time.Duration.ofMinutes(1));
        assertThat(oldSignatureOnlyCheck(signIn)).isTrue();             // the old code: signed in again
        authenticate(signIn).andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());      // its challenge was used up
    }

    @Test
    void aSignInAnsweredForAPhishingPageIsRefused() throws Exception {
        Device phone = passkeyFor("zoya");
        // tijori-login.example fetches a real challenge from Tijori and gets the passkey to answer it on its own page.
        ObjectNode relayed = phone.at("https://tijori-login.example").get(authenticationOptions());
        assertThat(oldSignatureOnlyCheck(relayed)).isTrue();
        authenticate(relayed).andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());     // clientDataJSON names the page that asked
    }

    @Test
    void aPasskeyMadeForAnotherSiteIsNotRegistered() throws Exception {
        String token = codeToken("zoya");
        // A look-alike page asks for a passkey for its own relying party, then hands the result to Tijori.
        ObjectNode forOtherSite = new Device().create(registrationOptions(token), "tijori-login.example");
        assertThat(WebAuthnManager.createNonStrictWebAuthnManager().parseRegistrationResponseJSON(forOtherSite.toString())).isNotNull();   // the old code stored any parsable key
        register(token, "Zoya's phone", forOtherSite).andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
        assertThat(jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM passkeys").query(Long.class).single()).isZero();
    }

    @Test
    void theRightAnswerSignsIn() throws Exception {
        // The control: same passkey, Tijori's own page, a fresh challenge.
        Device phone = passkeyFor("zoya");
        authenticate(phone.get(authenticationOptions())).andExpect(status().isOk());
    }
}

package com.tijori.passkeys;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import tools.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode;

import java.time.Duration;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Base64;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch;
import java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService;
import java.util.concurrent.Executors;
import java.util.concurrent.Future;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.get;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.header;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.status;

class PasskeySecurityTest extends ApiTest {

    @Test
    void noTokenIs401() throws Exception {
        mvc.perform(get("/accounts/me")).andExpect(status().isUnauthorized()).andExpect(header().string("WWW-Authenticate", "Bearer"));
        send("/webauthn/registration/options", null, "{}").andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());
    }

    @Test
    void addingAPasskeyNeedsASignInFromTheLastFiveMinutes() throws Exception {
        String token = codeToken("zoya");
        later(Duration.ofMinutes(5));   // the token itself is still valid for 10 minutes
        send("/webauthn/registration/options", token, "{}").andExpect(status().isForbidden()).andExpect(jsonPath("$.detail").value("Sign in again to add a passkey"));
        me(token).andExpect(status().isOk());
    }

    @Test
    void aChallengeIssuedToAnotherCustomerCannotAddAPasskeyHere() throws Exception {
        String dev = codeToken("dev");
        String zoya = codeToken("zoya");
        ObjectNode madeOnDevsChallenge = new Device().create(registrationOptions(dev));
        register(zoya, "Not mine", madeOnDevsChallenge).andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
        assertThat(jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM passkeys").query(Long.class).single()).isZero();
    }

    @Test
    void aPasskeyCannotSayItBelongsToAnotherCustomer() throws Exception {
        Device devsPhone = passkeyFor("dev");
        ObjectNode signIn = devsPhone.get(authenticationOptions());
        byte[] zoyasHandle = jdbc.sql("SELECT user_handle FROM customers WHERE email = 'zoya@example.com'").query(byte[].class).single();
        ((ObjectNode) signIn.path("response")).put("userHandle", Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(zoyasHandle));
        authenticate(signIn).andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());   // the signature does not cover userHandle: the server must compare it
    }

    @Test
    void aChallengeExpiresAfterFiveMinutes() throws Exception {
        Device phone = passkeyFor("zoya");
        JsonNode options = authenticationOptions();
        later(Duration.ofMinutes(5).plusSeconds(1));
        authenticate(phone.get(options)).andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());
    }

    @Test
    void aCounterThatGoesBackwardsLooksLikeACloneAndIsRefused() throws Exception {
        Device key = passkeyOn(Device.securityKey(), "zoya");
        long atRegistration = jdbc.sql("SELECT sign_count FROM passkeys").query(Long.class).single();
        authenticate(key.get(authenticationOptions())).andExpect(status().isOk());
        assertThat(jdbc.sql("SELECT sign_count FROM passkeys").query(Long.class).single()).isGreaterThan(atRegistration);   // the key's new count is kept
        jdbc.sql("UPDATE passkeys SET sign_count = 1000").update();   // as if the real key had signed 1000 times: this one is a copy
        authenticate(key.get(authenticationOptions())).andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());
    }

    @Test
    void aCodeWorksOnceAndOnlyNearItsTime() throws Exception {
        String code = currentCode();
        codeSignIn("zoya@example.com", "zoya-demo-pass", code).andExpect(status().isOk());
        codeSignIn("zoya@example.com", "zoya-demo-pass", code).andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());     // already used
        later(Duration.ofSeconds(30));
        String previous = Totp.code(TOTP_SECRET, Totp.step(CLOCK.now.getEpochSecond()) - 1);
        assertThat(previous).isEqualTo(code);
        String now = currentCode();
        later(Duration.ofSeconds(30));
        codeSignIn("zoya@example.com", "zoya-demo-pass", now).andExpect(status().isOk());              // one step late: a slow phone clock
        String old = Totp.code(TOTP_SECRET, Totp.step(CLOCK.now.getEpochSecond()) - 2);
        codeSignIn("dev@example.com", "dev-demo-pass", old).andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());     // two steps late: no
    }

    @Test
    void tenParallelSignInsWithOneCodeGiveOneToken() throws Exception {
        String code = currentCode();
        CountDownLatch start = new CountDownLatch(1);
        List<Future<Integer>> results = new ArrayList<>();
        try (ExecutorService threads = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) {
            for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
                results.add(threads.submit(() -> {
                    start.await();
                    return codeSignIn("zoya@example.com", "zoya-demo-pass", code).andReturn().getResponse().getStatus();
                }));
            }
            start.countDown();
        }
        List<Integer> statuses = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Future<Integer> f : results) {
            statuses.add(f.get());
        }
        assertThat(statuses).containsOnly(200, 401).filteredOn(s -> s == 200).hasSize(1);
    }

    @Test
    void oddAnswersAre400Or401NeverAnError() throws Exception {
        passkeyFor("zoya");
        for (String body : new String[]{"{}", "{\"rawId\":\"!!\",\"response\":{}}", "{\"rawId\":\"' OR '1'='1\",\"response\":{\"clientDataJSON\":\"x\"}}",
                "{\"rawId\":\"" + "a".repeat(5000) + "\",\"response\":{\"clientDataJSON\":\"" + "b".repeat(5000) + "\"}}", "[]"}) {
            int s = send("/webauthn/authentication", null, body).andReturn().getResponse().getStatus();
            assertThat(s).as(body.length() > 60 ? body.substring(0, 60) : body).isIn(400, 401);
        }
        send("/webauthn/authentication", null, "not json").andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
    }
}

package com.tijori.passkeys;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.dao.DataIntegrityViolationException;
import tools.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.status;

/** The rules hold for every writer, not only this app: plain SQL straight to PostgreSQL, no Java checks on the way. */
class PasskeyDatabaseTest extends ApiTest {

    void violates(String constraint, String sql) {
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> jdbc.sql(sql).update()).isInstanceOf(DataIntegrityViolationException.class).hasMessageContaining(constraint);
    }

    static final String ZOYA = "(SELECT id FROM customers WHERE email = 'zoya@example.com')";

    @Test
    void challengeRulesHoldWithoutJava() {
        violates("webauthn_challenges_length", "INSERT INTO webauthn_challenges (challenge, purpose, created_at, expires_at) VALUES ('\\x0102', 'authentication', now(), now() + interval '1 minute')");
        violates("webauthn_challenges_purpose", "INSERT INTO webauthn_challenges (challenge, purpose, created_at, expires_at) VALUES (gen_random_bytes(32), 'payment', now(), now() + interval '1 minute')");
        violates("webauthn_challenges_registration_has_customer", "INSERT INTO webauthn_challenges (challenge, purpose, created_at, expires_at) VALUES (gen_random_bytes(32), 'registration', now(), now() + interval '1 minute')");
        violates("webauthn_challenges_expiry", "INSERT INTO webauthn_challenges (challenge, purpose, created_at, expires_at) VALUES (gen_random_bytes(32), 'authentication', now(), now() + interval '1 day')");
        violates("webauthn_challenges_used_in_time", "INSERT INTO webauthn_challenges (challenge, purpose, created_at, expires_at, used_at) VALUES (gen_random_bytes(32), 'authentication', now(), now() + interval '1 minute', now() - interval '1 hour')");
    }

    @Test
    void passkeyAndCustomerRulesHoldWithoutJava() {
        String passkey = "INSERT INTO passkeys (credential_id, customer_id, attested_credential_data, sign_count, label, created_at) VALUES ";
        violates("passkeys_credential_id_length", passkey + "('\\x01', " + ZOYA + ", '\\x00', 0, 'Phone', now())");
        violates("passkeys_sign_count_range", passkey + "(gen_random_bytes(16), " + ZOYA + ", '\\x00', -1, 'Phone', now())");
        violates("passkeys_label_length", passkey + "(gen_random_bytes(16), " + ZOYA + ", '\\x00', 0, '', now())");
        violates("customers_user_handle_length", "UPDATE customers SET user_handle = 'zoya@example.com' WHERE email = 'zoya@example.com'");
        violates("customers_totp_secret_length", "UPDATE customers SET totp_secret = '\\x0102' WHERE email = 'zoya@example.com'");
        violates("customers_balance_nonnegative", "UPDATE customers SET balance_paise = -1 WHERE email = 'zoya@example.com'");
        violates("customers_email_lower", "UPDATE customers SET email = 'Zoya@Example.com' WHERE email = 'zoya@example.com'");
    }

    /**
     * Registration is one transaction. If the passkey cannot be saved, the challenge is not used up either, so the
     * customer's phone can send the same answer again. (A failed check, by contrast, does use it up: see Security.)
     */
    @Test
    void aSaveThatFailsRollsBackAndTheSameAnswerCanBeSentAgain() throws Exception {
        String token = codeToken("zoya");
        ObjectNode answer = new Device().create(registrationOptions(token));
        jdbc.sql("""
                CREATE FUNCTION refuse_passkeys() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN RAISE EXCEPTION 'storage is down'; END $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
                CREATE TRIGGER refuse_passkeys BEFORE INSERT ON passkeys FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION refuse_passkeys()""").update();
        try {
            assertThatThrownBy(() -> register(token, "Zoya's phone", answer)).hasRootCauseMessage("ERROR: storage is down\n  Where: PL/pgSQL function refuse_passkeys() line 1 at RAISE");
        } finally {
            jdbc.sql("DROP TRIGGER refuse_passkeys ON passkeys; DROP FUNCTION refuse_passkeys()").update();
        }
        assertThat(jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM webauthn_challenges WHERE used_at IS NULL").query(Long.class).single()).isEqualTo(1);
        register(token, "Zoya's phone", answer).andExpect(status().isCreated());
    }

    @Test
    void aFailedCheckUsesUpTheChallenge() throws Exception {
        String token = codeToken("zoya");
        Device phone = new Device();
        ObjectNode forOtherSite = phone.create(registrationOptions(token), "tijori-login.example");
        register(token, "Zoya's phone", forOtherSite).andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
        assertThat(jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM webauthn_challenges WHERE used_at IS NULL").query(Long.class).single()).isZero();
    }
}

The emulated phone: authenticator and browser, at an origin.

package com.tijori.passkeys;

import com.webauthn4j.data.AttestationConveyancePreference;
import com.webauthn4j.data.AuthenticatorAssertionResponse;
import com.webauthn4j.data.AuthenticatorAttestationResponse;
import com.webauthn4j.data.AuthenticatorSelectionCriteria;
import com.webauthn4j.data.PublicKeyCredential;
import com.webauthn4j.data.PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions;
import com.webauthn4j.data.PublicKeyCredentialDescriptor;
import com.webauthn4j.data.PublicKeyCredentialParameters;
import com.webauthn4j.data.PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions;
import com.webauthn4j.data.PublicKeyCredentialRpEntity;
import com.webauthn4j.data.PublicKeyCredentialType;
import com.webauthn4j.data.PublicKeyCredentialUserEntity;
import com.webauthn4j.data.ResidentKeyRequirement;
import com.webauthn4j.data.UserVerificationRequirement;
import com.webauthn4j.data.attestation.statement.COSEAlgorithmIdentifier;
import com.webauthn4j.data.client.Origin;
import com.webauthn4j.data.client.challenge.DefaultChallenge;
import com.webauthn4j.test.authenticator.webauthn.NoneAttestationAuthenticator;
import com.webauthn4j.test.authenticator.webauthn.WebAuthnAuthenticatorAdaptor;
import com.webauthn4j.test.client.ClientPlatform;
import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;
import tools.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Base64;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * A phone: an authenticator (webauthn4j's emulator, with real keys and real signatures) and the browser in front of
 * it, at a web origin. It turns the server's options JSON into the JSON a browser would send back. By default its
 * signature counter stays 0, as synced passkeys commonly report; securityKey() counts up like a hardware key.
 */
final class Device {

    static final String TIJORI = "https://app.tijori.example";
    static final JsonMapper JSON = JsonMapper.builder().build();
    private static final Base64.Encoder B64 = Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding();
    private static final Base64.Decoder UNB64 = Base64.getUrlDecoder();

    final ClientPlatform browser;

    Device() {
        this(false);
    }

    private Device(boolean counting) {
        NoneAttestationAuthenticator authenticator = new NoneAttestationAuthenticator();
        authenticator.setCountUpEnabled(counting);
        browser = new ClientPlatform(new Origin(TIJORI), new WebAuthnAuthenticatorAdaptor(authenticator));
    }

    static Device securityKey() {
        return new Device(true);
    }

    /** The same authenticator, but the page asking is at another origin (a phishing page, or a client that lies). */
    Device at(String origin) {
        browser.setOrigin(new Origin(origin));
        return this;
    }

    /** navigator.credentials.create(options), as JSON. rpIdOverride plays a page that asks for another relying party. */
    ObjectNode create(JsonNode o, String rpIdOverride) {
        List<PublicKeyCredentialParameters> algs = new ArrayList<>();
        o.path("pubKeyCredParams").forEach(p -> algs.add(new PublicKeyCredentialParameters(PublicKeyCredentialType.PUBLIC_KEY, COSEAlgorithmIdentifier.create(p.path("alg").asLong()))));
        List<PublicKeyCredentialDescriptor> exclude = new ArrayList<>();
        o.path("excludeCredentials").forEach(c -> exclude.add(new PublicKeyCredentialDescriptor(PublicKeyCredentialType.PUBLIC_KEY, UNB64.decode(c.path("id").asString()), null)));
        PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions options = new PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions(
                new PublicKeyCredentialRpEntity(rpIdOverride != null ? rpIdOverride : o.path("rp").path("id").asString(), o.path("rp").path("name").asString()),
                new PublicKeyCredentialUserEntity(UNB64.decode(o.path("user").path("id").asString()), o.path("user").path("name").asString(), o.path("user").path("displayName").asString()),
                new DefaultChallenge(UNB64.decode(o.path("challenge").asString())), algs, o.path("timeout").asLong(), exclude,
                new AuthenticatorSelectionCriteria(null, ResidentKeyRequirement.REQUIRED, UserVerificationRequirement.REQUIRED),
                AttestationConveyancePreference.NONE, null);
        PublicKeyCredential<AuthenticatorAttestationResponse, ?> credential = browser.create(options);
        ObjectNode json = base(credential.getRawId());
        json.putObject("response").put("clientDataJSON", B64.encodeToString(credential.getResponse().getClientDataJSON()))
                .put("attestationObject", B64.encodeToString(credential.getResponse().getAttestationObject())).putArray("transports").add("internal");
        return json;
    }

    ObjectNode create(JsonNode options) {
        return create(options, null);
    }

    /** navigator.credentials.get(options), as JSON. */
    ObjectNode get(JsonNode o) {
        PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions options = new PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions(new DefaultChallenge(UNB64.decode(o.path("challenge").asString())),
                o.path("timeout").asLong(), o.path("rpId").asString(), List.of(), UserVerificationRequirement.REQUIRED, null);
        PublicKeyCredential<AuthenticatorAssertionResponse, ?> credential = browser.get(options);
        ObjectNode json = base(credential.getRawId());
        json.putObject("response").put("clientDataJSON", B64.encodeToString(credential.getResponse().getClientDataJSON()))
                .put("authenticatorData", B64.encodeToString(credential.getResponse().getAuthenticatorData()))
                .put("signature", B64.encodeToString(credential.getResponse().getSignature()))
                .put("userHandle", B64.encodeToString(credential.getResponse().getUserHandle()));
        return json;
    }

    private static ObjectNode base(byte[] rawId) {
        ObjectNode json = JSON.createObjectNode().put("id", B64.encodeToString(rawId)).put("rawId", B64.encodeToString(rawId)).put("type", "public-key");
        json.putObject("clientExtensionResults");
        return json;
    }
}

package com.tijori.passkeys;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.boot.webmvc.test.autoconfigure.AutoConfigureMockMvc;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Import;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.test.context.bean.override.convention.TestBean;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.MockMvc;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.ResultActions;
import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;
import tools.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode;

import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.ZoneId;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;

import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.get;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.post;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.status;

/**
 * Shared setup: the whole app on a real PostgreSQL, a test signing key, a clock the tests move, and before each test
 * the two demo customers with no passkeys, no challenges and no used codes.
 */
@SpringBootTest(properties = "tijori.jwt.secret=" + ApiTest.SECRET)
@AutoConfigureMockMvc
@Import(PostgresTestConfig.class)
abstract class ApiTest {

    static final String SECRET = "dGVzdC1vbmx5LXRpam9yaS1hY2Nlc3MtdG9rZW4ta2V5LTI1Ni1iaXRzLW9yLW1vcmU";
    static final byte[] TOTP_SECRET = "12345678901234567890".getBytes(StandardCharsets.US_ASCII);   // RFC 6238's test secret, as in V2
    static final Instant START = Instant.parse("2026-10-19T06:00:00Z");
    static final JsonMapper JSON = JsonMapper.builder().build();

    static final class TestClock extends Clock {
        Instant now = START;

        @Override
        public ZoneId getZone() {
            return ZoneOffset.UTC;
        }

        @Override
        public Clock withZone(ZoneId zone) {
            return this;
        }

        @Override
        public Instant instant() {
            return now;
        }
    }

    static final TestClock CLOCK = new TestClock();

    @TestBean
    Clock clock;

    static Clock clock() {
        return CLOCK;
    }

    @Autowired
    MockMvc mvc;
    @Autowired
    JdbcClient jdbc;

    @BeforeEach
    void cleanSlate() {
        CLOCK.now = START;
        jdbc.sql("DELETE FROM passkeys").update();
        jdbc.sql("DELETE FROM webauthn_challenges").update();
        jdbc.sql("UPDATE customers SET totp_last_step = NULL").update();
    }

    void later(Duration d) {
        CLOCK.now = CLOCK.now.plus(d);
    }

    /** The code the customer's authenticator app shows right now. */
    static String currentCode() {
        return Totp.code(TOTP_SECRET, Totp.step(CLOCK.now.getEpochSecond()));
    }

    ResultActions codeSignIn(String email, String password, String code) throws Exception {
        return mvc.perform(post("/2fa/totp").contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
                .content("{\"email\":\"%s\",\"password\":\"%s\",\"code\":\"%s\"}".formatted(email, password, code)));
    }

    /** A sign-in with password and code that must work; then the clock moves past that code's 30 seconds. */
    String codeToken(String member) throws Exception {
        String token = body(codeSignIn(member + "@example.com", member + "-demo-pass", currentCode()).andExpect(status().isOk())).get("accessToken").asString();
        later(Duration.ofSeconds(30));
        return token;
    }

    ResultActions send(String path, String token, String json) throws Exception {
        var request = org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.post(path).contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON).content(json);
        return mvc.perform(token == null ? request : request.header("Authorization", "Bearer " + token));
    }

    JsonNode registrationOptions(String token) throws Exception {
        return body(send("/webauthn/registration/options", token, "{}").andExpect(status().isOk()));
    }

    ResultActions register(String token, String label, ObjectNode credential) throws Exception {
        ObjectNode body = JSON.createObjectNode().put("label", label);
        body.set("credential", credential);
        return send("/webauthn/registration", token, body.toString());
    }

    /** A passkey on this device for this customer, through the real registration. */
    Device passkeyFor(String member) throws Exception {
        return passkeyOn(new Device(), member);
    }

    Device passkeyOn(Device phone, String member) throws Exception {
        String token = codeToken(member);
        register(token, member + "'s phone", phone.create(registrationOptions(token))).andExpect(status().isCreated());
        return phone;
    }

    JsonNode authenticationOptions() throws Exception {
        return body(send("/webauthn/authentication/options", null, "{}").andExpect(status().isOk()));
    }

    ResultActions authenticate(ObjectNode assertion) throws Exception {
        return send("/webauthn/authentication", null, assertion.toString());
    }

    ResultActions me(String token) throws Exception {
        return mvc.perform(get("/accounts/me").header("Authorization", "Bearer " + token));
    }

    static JsonNode body(ResultActions result) throws Exception {
        return JSON.readTree(result.andReturn().getResponse().getContentAsString());
    }
}

import java.util.Base64;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

@RestController
class PasskeyListController {

    private final JdbcClient jdbc;

    PasskeyListController(JdbcClient jdbc) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
    }

    @GetMapping("/webauthn/passkeys")
    List<Map<String, String>> list(@AuthenticationPrincipal Jwt jwt) {
        return jdbc.sql("SELECT credential_id, label FROM passkeys WHERE customer_id = ? ORDER BY created_at").param(Long.parseLong(jwt.getSubject()))
                .query((rs, n) -> Map.of("id", Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(rs.getBytes(1)), "label", rs.getString(2))).list();
    }

    /** The customer is part of the query: another customer's passkey finds no row, like an unknown one. */
    @DeleteMapping("/webauthn/passkeys/{id}")
    @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.NO_CONTENT)
    void remove(@AuthenticationPrincipal Jwt jwt, @PathVariable String id) {
        byte[] credentialId;
        try {
            credentialId = Base64.getUrlDecoder().decode(id);
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException notBase64) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No such passkey");
        }
        if (jdbc.sql("DELETE FROM passkeys WHERE credential_id = ? AND customer_id = ?").params(credentialId, Long.parseLong(jwt.getSubject())).update() == 0) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No such passkey");
        }
    }
}

package com.tijori.passkeys;

import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.http.HttpMethod;
import org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.builders.HttpSecurity;
import org.springframework.security.config.http.SessionCreationPolicy;
import org.springframework.security.crypto.factory.PasswordEncoderFactories;
import org.springframework.security.crypto.password.PasswordEncoder;
import org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain;

@Configuration
class SecurityConfig {

    /** The sign-in ceremonies are open (they are the proof); adding a passkey and the account need a token. */
    @Bean
    SecurityFilterChain api(HttpSecurity http, ProblemResponses problems) throws Exception {
        http.authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a
                        .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.POST, "/2fa/totp", "/webauthn/authentication/options", "/webauthn/authentication").permitAll()
                        .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.POST, "/webauthn/registration/options", "/webauthn/registration").hasAuthority("SCOPE_accounts")
                        .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/accounts/me", "/webauthn/passkeys").hasAuthority("SCOPE_accounts")
                        .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.DELETE, "/webauthn/passkeys/*").hasAuthority("SCOPE_accounts")
                        .requestMatchers("/error").permitAll()   // otherwise a server error is forwarded here and shown as a 401
                        .anyRequest().denyAll())
                .oauth2ResourceServer(o -> o.jwt(jwt -> {}).authenticationEntryPoint(problems::unauthenticated).accessDeniedHandler(problems::forbidden))
                .exceptionHandling(x -> x.authenticationEntryPoint(problems::unauthenticated).accessDeniedHandler(problems::forbidden))
                .sessionManagement(s -> s.sessionCreationPolicy(SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS))
                .csrf(csrf -> csrf.disable());   // no cookies: the token travels in a header the browser never adds by itself
        return http.build();
    }

    @Bean
    PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder() {
        return PasswordEncoderFactories.createDelegatingPasswordEncoder();
    }
}

package com.tijori.passkeys;

import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.security.crypto.password.PasswordEncoder;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;

import java.security.MessageDigest;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.time.OffsetDateTime;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Optional;

/** The fallback: password and a code from an authenticator app. Never a password alone, never an SMS. */
@Service
class CodeSignIn {

    private final JdbcClient jdbc;
    private final PasswordEncoder encoder;
    private final Clock clock;
    private final String dummyHash;

    CodeSignIn(JdbcClient jdbc, PasswordEncoder encoder, Clock clock) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
        this.encoder = encoder;
        this.clock = clock;
        this.dummyHash = encoder.encode("no-such-customer");
    }

    private record Customer(long id, String passwordHash, byte[] totpSecret) {
    }

    /** Demo rule: 5 wrong codes in a row lock code sign-in for 15 minutes. */
    static final int MAX_WRONG_CODES = 5;
    static final Duration LOCK = Duration.ofMinutes(15);

    /**
     * The customer's id if the password is right, code sign-in is not locked, and the code is the current one (or
     * the one before) and unused. A wrong code counts (a used one does not: it is a replay, not a guess); the fifth locks; a good sign-in resets the count.
     */
    @Transactional
    Optional<Long> signIn(String email, String password, String code) {
        Optional<Customer> customer = jdbc.sql("SELECT id, password_hash, totp_secret FROM customers WHERE email = ? FOR UPDATE")
                .param(email.strip().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)).query(Customer.class).optional();
        boolean passwordOk = encoder.matches(password, customer.map(Customer::passwordHash).orElse(dummyHash));
        if (customer.isEmpty() || !passwordOk) {
            return Optional.empty();
        }
        long id = customer.get().id();
        OffsetDateTime now = OffsetDateTime.ofInstant(clock.instant(), ZoneOffset.UTC);
        if (jdbc.sql("SELECT codes_locked_until > ? FROM customers WHERE id = ?").params(now, id).query(Boolean.class).optional().orElse(false)) {
            return Optional.empty();   // the same answer as a wrong code: nothing tells a guesser they are locked out
        }
        long step = Totp.step(now.toEpochSecond());
        for (long s = step; s >= step - 1; s--) {
            if (MessageDigest.isEqual(Totp.code(customer.get().totpSecret(), s).getBytes(StandardCharsets.US_ASCII), code.getBytes(StandardCharsets.US_ASCII))) {
                Optional<Long> ok = jdbc.sql("UPDATE customers SET totp_last_step = ?, failed_codes = 0, codes_locked_until = NULL WHERE id = ? AND (totp_last_step IS NULL OR totp_last_step < ?) RETURNING id")
                        .params(s, id, s).query(Long.class).optional();
                return ok;   // empty if already used: a replay, not a guess, so it does not count
            }
        }
        jdbc.sql("""
                UPDATE customers SET failed_codes = CASE WHEN failed_codes + 1 >= ? THEN 0 ELSE failed_codes + 1 END,
                                     codes_locked_until = CASE WHEN failed_codes + 1 >= ? THEN ? ELSE codes_locked_until END
                WHERE id = ?""").params(MAX_WRONG_CODES, MAX_WRONG_CODES, now.plus(LOCK), id).update();
        return Optional.empty();
    }
}
